The diagram above shows a unit circle and the angle $\theta $ measured in the usual way. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $0.91,$ calculate the reference angle ${\theta }_{R}$ to the nearest integer.

${\theta }_{R}≈$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
question.worked_solution:
The reference angle is the angle that $\theta $ makes with the $x$-axis.

First, we create a right-triangle by drawing a vertical line from $P$ to the $x$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/6f87f2f8bd98ca123c4bc524b6f0e85dada9064b9bbb2c360904c6217a36fb61.png)

So, we have the following triangle, where ${\theta }_{R}$ is the reference angle of $\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/c024d98c0a2d2be7f4c198ffc108e6fbfc5707047608733f07fea72602f04294.png)

We know that the hypotenuse has a length of $1$ because it is a radius of the unit circle. 

Now, using the triangle above, we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{\theta }_{R}=\frac{0.91}{1}=0.91.
$$

Now, we compute the angle ${\theta }_{R}$ using the inverse sine:

$$
{\theta }_{R}=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(0.91)≈{66}^{∘}
$$
